key_insight: FREDI jointly optimizes fair wireless resource allocation and dual-threshold early-exit inference to securely offload only critical events in cooperative edge intelligence.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical way to balance latency, fairness, security, and compute efficiency in UE–edge–cloud deployments for event-triggered AI.
method: Proportional-fair utility maximization over UE–ES association, bandwidth, power, and confidence thresholds
Dual-threshold early-exit CNN screening at the UE to decide local acceptance vs secure offload
Exact optimization via set-monotone critical-event structure, finite confidence-domain search, and mixed-integer exponential-cone programming
evidence_signal: Experiments with early-exit MobileNetV2 and ShuffleNetV2 report near-perfect UE fairness, aggregate utility close to a Sum-Utility benchmark, and Stage-A scaling from 6 to 144 UEs with median solve times below 0.1 s in tested cases.
watch_item: The method relies on empirical confidence distributions and certified solver formulations, so performance and tractability may depend on dataset behavior, threshold granularity, and deployment-scale problem size.
paper_title: Proportional-Fair Resource Allocation and Dual-Threshold Early-Exit Inference for Secure Cooperative Multi-Layer Edge Intelligence
